title: Made a small iOS RPG with Claude, looking for a few testers
author: Clean_Channel5307
selftext:
I'm Florian, I make small iOS apps in Vienna. This week I released Das Tal ohne Wiederkehr (The Valley of No Return), a little RPG in German and English.

  
I didn't write the code. I gave Claude the story, the quest ideas, the mood and the art style, and Claude built it. Then I played, sent things back, played again. More director than programmer.

  
The worst part was water. For a long time the lake floated in mid-air and the waterfall looked like anything but a waterfall.

  
Chapter 1 is playable now. You arrive in a closed-off valley, meet three camps and make it to the trading day. Chapters 2 to 5 will come as updates. The game is free, no ads, no in-app purchases, no account. Needs iOS 17 and an A12 or newer.

  
If you play it, I'm mostly curious whether you find your way without a map arrow, whether the fights have a good rhythm, whether the story makes sense, how it runs on older iPhones, and whether saving and picking a camp are clear.

  
[https://apps.apple.com/app/id6813633319](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6813633319)

  
I'll answer in the comments.

comments.author: ipreuss
comments.body:
I'll take a look – it's downloading right now.

First feedback on the store page: the texts clearly sound like AI. That makes it unattractive. You might want to write them yourself, or experiment with other models or better prompts.

I'm currently working on an RPG myself, and the texts are a challenge. Luckily, I managed to recruit my niece as a writer. https://github.com/ipreuss/tending-roots

replies.author: Clean_Channel5307
replies.body:
Maybe your niece wants to write mine as well :)

Seriously, no joke, it is a problem. Also with the translation.

I find the writing of Rings of Power terrible as well (loving the books). Hopefully mine isn't that bad.

Thank you

comments.author: Clean_Channel5307
comments.body:
Thanks a lot for actually playing it and writing all this down.

  
The camera in curves and the guide not waiting are on my list now.

  
The rude villagers were actually the plan. I tried to lean a bit on Gothic, the rough tone and the zero to hero idea. Maybe I overdid it at the start.

comments.author: Clean_Channel5307
comments.body:
You were right about the store text. I wrote a new description on itch, in my own words:

[https://fmahrl80.itch.io/das-tal-ohne-wiederkehr](https://fmahrl80.itch.io/das-tal-ohne-wiederkehr)

The valley has filled out since you tried it. There are wanderers and robbers on the roads now, the monks sing the hours in the monastery, and at night people sit by the fire and talk. Over 600 new lines are voiced, in German and in English.

There is a Windows build on itch as well, still free. If you ever open it again, I would like to know whether it feels less empty.

replies.author: ipreuss
replies.body: It feeling empty wasn’t my complaint.

replies.author: Clean_Channel5307
replies.body: Fair point, I mixed that up. Yours was the camera in curves, the guide not waiting, items that do nothing yet and the rude villagers. Thanks for the correction.
